'''Geoffrey Thomas Bennett''' [[OBE]] (1868–1943) was an English [[mathematician]], professor at the [[University of Cambridge]].

== Life and work ==
Born in London,<ref>G. T. Bennett's father was a [[wiktionary:gold-beater|gold-beater]] in London. {{acad|id=BNT887GT|name=Bennett, Geoffrey Thomas}}</ref><ref>Sir Norman Godfrey Bennett (1870–1947) was Geoffrey Thomas Bennett's brother. {{acad|id=BNT888NG|name=Bennett, Norman Godfrey}}</ref> he began his secondary studies at the [[University College School]], under [[Robert Tucker (mathematician)|Robert Tucker]]. After one year at [[University College of London]], Bennett obtained a scholarship at [[St. John's College, Cambridge]], where he graduated in 1890 as [[Senior Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|Senior Wrangler]]. However, the best grade in the [[Mathematical Tripos]] of that year was for [[Philippa Fawcett]], but she was not included in the list for her gender.{{sfn | Baker | 1944 | p=597 }}

Upon completion of his studies he was appointed college lecturer of mathematics at [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge]]. He held a fellowship at the college from 1893 until his death in 1943.{{sfn | Frederickson | 2002 | p=152 }} He had also great interest in music and athletics. He was a keen bicyclist and a good pianist.{{sfn | Baker | 1944 | p=598 }}

During the [[First World War]] he was member of the Anti-Aircraft Experimental Section (AAES) for his versatility  and for his ability solving geometrical problems by mechanical means.{{sfn | Barrow-Green | 2014 | p=91 }}
